title: Who enters scored rounds again and again
question: Which firms and housing sponsors apply round after round, and how often do they win?
finding: Scooter permits: 8 firms applied in two or more of the 3 rounds; Scoot was permitted in 2 of 2, Lime was permitted in 1 of 2, Spin was permitted in 1 of 2, JUMP was permitted in 1 of 2, Skip was permitted in 1 of 2 rounds with a published decision. State housing credits: 15 sponsors each stand behind two or more San Francisco applications; the most frequent are Mercy Housing California (17 applications, 9 funded); Related Affordable (15 applications, 9 funded); San Francisco Housing Development Corporation (10 applications, 6 funded). 4 developments applied three or more times before being funded or are still trying.
how: Scooter firms are counted by the name on the applicant lists. Housing sponsors are the parent companies the State prints beside each general partner, pooled across every list that names the development; where no parent is printed, the general partner’s own name is used, and an abbreviation in a partnership’s name is joined to a parent only when a State row prints both. A development with two partners counts for both; 15 applications print no partner at all and are left out of the sponsor rows. An application is one entry in one round; "funded" counts applications in an award or recommendation list. Lobbying entries are filings in the City’s lobbyist directory that name the brand as client.
limits: Repeat winners are no surprise in a scored round. The same few sponsors appear on most San Francisco applications in these lists, a site’s developer may be settled locally before any State application, and a project that loses can come back with a stronger application, as several in this table did. Scooter permits went to the highest scores. Lobbying is reported because the firms filed it; brand names are matched as words and one brand can be two companies over time. Sponsor families are read from names: two partnerships with similar names may be unrelated.
